newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: HOCKEY-VEEN GOAL GIVES DUTCH OPENING WIN.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-VEEN GOAL GIVES DUTCH OPENING WIN.

text.p: A cheeky individual goal by Dutch captain Stephan Veen enabled the Olympic champions to beat Australia 3-2 after twice coming from behind in the opening match of the Golden Jubilee hockey tournament on Sunday.

But hosts Pakistan, hoping to celebrate the country's 50th jubilee by winning the five-nation event, disappointed their supporters when they were held to a 1-1 draw by an inexperienced but spirited England side.
Australia, Olympic bronze medallists, twice went ahead but Veen ensured the Netherlands maintained their unbeaten record since the Atlanta Games with his 55th-minute goal.
Veen jinked his way through a crowded circle before forcing the ball into the net.
The Netherlands had looked in some danger after Australia went ahead in the fourth minute when Stephen Davies lobbed the ball over the Dutch goalkeeper from the back line for Baeden Choppy to score.
The next three goals all came from penalty corners, Bram Lomans coming on to score twice for the Dutch and Jay Stacy, the Australian captain scoring in between.
Pakistan were denied by some outstanding goalkeeping by England goalkeeper David Luckes.

Against the run of play Russell Garcia, the new England captain, gave his side the lead on the half hour. Pakistan levelled right on the interval with a shot into the roof of the net by inside left Muhammad Shahbaz.
